context.full_target:
The complete Theorem 1 (Logarithm-free convergence), with its Section 2 standing definitions and fixed scheme, on PDF page 2.

Use the periodic domain mathbbT = reals/(2*pi*integers) with normalized measure dx/(2*pi). For a periodic function f, hat f(k) = (2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx and <k> = (1+k^2)^(1/2). The Sobolev norm is ||f||_(H^s)^2 = sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2*s) |hat f(k)|^2. These spaces are completions of trigonometric polynomials in these norms, with negative-order spaces interpreted as distributions. Reality means hat f(-k) = conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0) = 0. Time suprema use continuous representatives; derivative norms use essential suprema.

Let S_t = exp(-t*partial_x^3), with Fourier multiplier exp(i*t*k^3). Let P0 be the spatial mean and P = I-P0. Let D^(-1) = partial_x^(-1) have multiplier (i*k)^(-1) for k != 0 and zero at k=0, and D^(-2) = (D^(-1))^2. The equation is
  u_t + u_xxx = (1/2)*partial_x(u^2), u(0)=u0.
The exact solution is the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) distributional solution obtained by smooth approximation.

For timestep tau=T/L, the time-semidiscrete scheme is exactly
  u^0 = u0,
  u^(n+1) = S_tau u^n + F_tau(u^n) + H_tau(u^n),
where all products below are spatial products and [G(s)]_(s=0)^(s=tau) means G(tau)-G(0):
  F_tau(f) = (1/6)*P[(S_tau D^(-1) f)^2]
             - (1/6)*S_tau P[(D^(-1) f)^2],
  H_tau(f) = (1/3)*P[(S_tau D^(-1) f)*D^(-1) F_tau(f)]
             + (tau/9)*(S_tau D^(-1) f)*P0(f^2)
             - (1/54)*[S_(tau-s) D^(-1)[(S_s D^(-1) f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)
             - (1/(27*tau))*[S_(tau-s) D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau) D^(-2) F_tau(f))*(S_s D^(-1) f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau).
This is the source scheme (2), with no spatial frequency cutoff.

For every T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0, there exist C>0 and tau0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that, for every real mean-zero u0 in H^gamma(mathbbT) with ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0, this fixed scheme satisfies
  max_(0<=n<=L) ||u(n*tau)-u^n||_(L^2) <= C*tau^gamma.
The constants are uniform over the entire stated initial-data ball and all permitted timesteps, with no Fourier-support restriction. The target includes all the hypotheses, quantifiers, endpoints, solution convention and method above.
context.conclusion: There exist positive constants C and tau0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that, for every real mean-zero u0 in H^gamma(Ttor) with ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0, the exact KdV solution in D012 exists and the unmodified unfiltered scheme D009–D011 is well defined and satisfies max_(0<=n<=L)||u(n*tau)-u^n||_(L2)<=C*tau^gamma. These constants are uniform on the entire initial-data ball, all permitted timesteps, and all Fourier supports, with the domain, normalized measure, Fourier/Sobolev conventions, Airy group, projections, inverse derivatives and full Ftau,Htau formula fixed in D001–D012.

record.definition: Ttor = reals/(2*pi*integers), with normalized measure dx/(2*pi); spatial products and integrals are on this domain.
For an integrable periodic f, Fourier(f)(k)=hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx; the transform extends to distributions by duality.

For every real s, H^s(Ttor) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials with ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2, <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2). Negative spaces are interpreted as distributions. Homogeneous norms on zero-mean distributions are ||f||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2. Real means hat f(-k)=conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0)=0.

L2=H^0(Ttor), with ||f||_2^2=(2*pi)^(-1) integral |f|^2 dx. More generally L^p uses the same normalized measure; L^infinity is essential supremum. Sequence ell^2 uses counting measure on Z (or Z\{0} when specified). Time suprema use continuous representatives; derivative norms are essential suprema.

record.type: Airy group indexed by real time
record.definition: S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), hat(S_t f)(k)=exp(i*t*k^3) hat f(k).
P0(f)=hat f(0), identified with a constant function.
Pnz=I-P0, denoted P in the supplied proof. Fourier projections P_leq(N) and P_gt(N) retain |k|<=N and |k|>N respectively, for N>=0.
Dinv=partial_x^(-1) has Fourier multiplier (i*k)^(-1) at nonzero integer k and zero at k=0. Dinv2=(Dinv)^2 is denoted D^(-2).

record.type: quadratic update family for positive timestep
record.definition: For tau>0 and mean-zero f in L2, Ftau(f)=(1/6)*Pnz[(S_tau Dinv f)^2]-(1/6)*S_tau Pnz[(Dinv f)^2].

record.type: cubic update family for positive timestep
record.definition: For tau>0 and mean-zero f in L2, Htau(f)=(1/3)*Pnz[(S_tau Dinv f)*Dinv Ftau(f)]+(tau/9)*(S_tau Dinv f)*P0(f^2)-(1/54)*[S_(tau-s) Dinv[(S_s Dinv f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)-(1/(27*tau))*[S_(tau-s) Dinv2[(S_(s-tau) Dinv2 Ftau(f))*(S_s Dinv f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau). Brackets mean the value at tau minus the value at zero. All products are spatial products.

For every positive tau, Psi_tau(f)=S_tau f+Ftau(f)+Htau(f) on mean-zero L2 data. Given such tau, mean-zero u0 in L2 and an integer L>=1, set t_n=n*tau, u^0=u0 and u^(n+1)=Psi_tau(u^n) for 0<=n<L; write v^n=S_(-t_n)u^n. For the target with T>0, specialize tau=T/L. There is no spatial cutoff.

KdV is u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)*partial_x(u^2), u(0)=u0. An exact solution on [0,T] with H^gamma data means the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma(Ttor)) distributional solution obtained by smooth approximation. This describes the convention and asserts no existence. For such a solution write v(t)=S_(-t)u(t), and M=1+sup_[0,T]||v(t)||_(H^gamma).
For tau>0 and real alpha,beta, M_tau g=tau^(-1) integral_0^tau g(s) ds and eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).

record.type: averaged cubic trilinear Fourier family, initially on polynomials
record.definition: For tau>0, t0 real, and mean-zero polynomial inputs f1,f2,f3, define Remainder_(t0,tau)(f1,f2,f3) to have zero mean and, for k!=0, Fourier coefficient -tau/(18*i*k) sum_(a+b+c=k,a+b!=0) exp(-i*t0*Phi)*eta_tau(alpha,beta)*hat f1(a)*hat f2(b)*hat f3(c), where p=a+b, alpha=3*a*b*p, beta=3*k*c*p and Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3. Its bounded extensions will be proved; R^n_(2,tau) means t0=t_n.
For nonzero integers a,b,c,d with a+b+c+d=0, let N1>=N2>=N3>=N4 be the decreasing rearrangement of |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|, and Third(a,b,c,d)=N3. Ties may be ordered arbitrarily.
Bop_t(f,g)=S_(-t)*partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)], initially for smooth periodic functions and by distributional product for L2 inputs.
Jop_t(f,g)=S_(-t) Pnz[(S_t Dinv f)(S_t Dinv g)].

For a time interval I=[a,b], Cop_I(f,g,h)=integral_a^b S_(-t) Pnz{Pnz[(S_t f(t))(S_t g(t))]*(S_t Dinv h(t))} dt. Initially this is defined for smooth inputs; the continuous extensions in the source estimates are meant when used for rough inputs.
pstar=23/14.

For an interval I of length at most one, ||f||_X(I)=||f||_(L^infinity(I;L2))+||partial_t f||_(L^infinity(I;H^(-pstar))). Derivatives are distributional time derivatives, with their essential-supremum norms.

For a grid start t_n=n*tau, tau>0, and time-independent mean-zero w, Stage_n(t;w)=(1/2) integral_(t_n)^t Bop_s(w,w) ds for t in [t_n,t_n+tau]. The associated bilinear stage has w1,w2 in its two slots.
For 0<gamma<=1, agamma=1/2-gamma if gamma<1/2, agamma=1/8 if gamma=1/2, and agamma=0 if gamma>1/2.

For smooth mean-zero initial data and tau=T/L>0, on I_n=[t_n,t_(n+1)] put f_n=v^n, F_n(t)=Stage_n(t;f_n), z_n(t)=f_n+F_n(t), C_n(t)=integral_(t_n)^t Bop_s(f_n,F_n(s)) ds, Q_n(t)=(1/2)integral_(t_n)^t Bop_s(F_n(s),F_n(s)) ds, W_n=Q_n(t_(n+1))+Remainder_(t_n,tau)(f_n,f_n,f_n), V(t)=f_n+F_n(t)+C_n(t)+Q_n(t)-(t-t_n)*W_n/tau, and Y_n(t)=V(t)-z_n(t). Put rho_n(t)=-integral_(t_n)^t Bop_s(Y_n,z_n) ds-(1/2)integral_(t_n)^t Bop_s(Y_n,Y_n) ds-(t-t_n)*W_n/tau. Define Rres(0)=0 and concatenate rho_n: Rres(t)=sum_(j<n)rho_j(t_(j+1))+rho_n(t) on I_n. For an exact twisted solution v, set e=v-V, delta_n=||f_n-v(t_n)||_2, q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n. V is initially stepwise defined; continuity is a proved assertion. The per-step formulas define a tuple of functions for any prescribed smooth mean-zero step state f_n, step start n*tau and positive tau, independently of whether f_n comes from a full trajectory. In that local use, any comparison state w may replace v(t_n) in delta_n=||f_n-w||_2 and q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n. Full concatenation, V on the whole time interval and e=v-V concern a full numerical trajectory and an exact solution as specified above.

record.statement: For the real mean-zero normalized 2*pi-periodic source equation U_t=U U_x+U_xxx, use the source twisted coefficients y_k(t)=exp(i*k^3*t) hat U(k,t), k!=0, with ||y||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2*s)|y_k|^2. for s>=0, finite T_s>0, initial dot H^s datum y0 and an upper bound B0 for its L2 norm, the source Galerkin flows have sup_[0,T_s] dot H^s norm bounded by a constant depending only on s,T_s,||y0||_(dot H^s),B0, uniformly in Galerkin dimension. For s>0 a subsequence converges to a distributional limiting solution with the same bound (the limiting statement uses strong L^p_t H^sigma convergence for 0<sigma<s and 1<p<infinity and weak-star L^infinity_t dot H^s convergence). The uniqueness and continuity claims for s>1/2 and for 0<s<=1/2 make this solution unique, C([0,T_s];dot H^s), L2 conserving and Lipschitz continuous in the initial dot H^s data. At s=0, for s=0 there is a unique C([0,T_s];dot H^0) solution obtained by smooth approximation and Lipschitz continuous in the initial data. For the two-flow estimate, for theta in (-1,0], if ||y0||_2+||z0||_2<=B, then their two source twisted flows satisfy sup_[0,T_s]||y-z||_(dot H^theta)<=C'(B,theta)*C_B(theta)^(T_s)*||y0-z0||_(dot H^theta). All these claims concern the source equation and its twist, not the target sign convention.

source.title: On the regularization mechanism for the periodic Korteweg–de Vries equation
source.source_statement: For the real mean-zero normalized 2*pi-periodic source equation U_t=U U_x+U_xxx, use the source twisted coefficients y_k(t)=exp(i*k^3*t) hat U(k,t), k!=0, with ||y||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2*s)|y_k|^2. Theorems 4.2–4.3: for s>=0, finite T_s>0, initial dot H^s datum y0 and an upper bound B0 for its L2 norm, the source Galerkin flows have sup_[0,T_s] dot H^s norm bounded by a constant depending only on s,T_s,||y0||_(dot H^s),B0, uniformly in Galerkin dimension. For s>0 a subsequence converges to a distributional limiting solution with the same bound (Theorem 4.3 uses strong L^p_t H^sigma convergence for 0<sigma<s and 1<p<infinity and weak-star L^infinity_t dot H^s convergence). Theorem 5.1 for s>1/2 and Theorem 6.3 for 0<s<=1/2 make this solution unique, C([0,T_s];dot H^s), L2 conserving and Lipschitz continuous in the initial dot H^s data. Theorem 6.4: for s=0 there is a unique C([0,T_s];dot H^0) solution obtained by smooth approximation and Lipschitz continuous in the initial data. Theorem 6.5: for theta in (-1,0], if ||y0||_2+||z0||_2<=B, then their two source twisted flows satisfy sup_[0,T_s]||y-z||_(dot H^theta)<=C'(B,theta)*C_B(theta)^(T_s)*||y0-z0||_(dot H^theta). All these claims concern the source equation and its twist, not the target sign convention.
hypotheses: Real mean-zero source data in dot H^s, s>=0, and a finite positive time interval.
The bound for the dot H^s flow uses only an upper bound for the initial L2 and dot H^s norms.
For the last Lipschitz estimate theta is in (-1,0] and the two initial L2 norms have sum at most B.

record.statement: Let alpha_s in [0,1] and 0<=a_s<=b_s with b_s-a_s<=1. For three functions g_j in L^infinity([a_s,b_s];H^alpha_s) with partial_t g_j in L^infinity([a_s,b_s];H^(-23/14)), define Csrc(g1,g2,g3)=integral_(a_s)^(b_s) exp(t partial_x^3) Pnz{Pnz[(exp(-t partial_x^3)g1)(exp(-t partial_x^3)g2)]*(exp(-t partial_x^3)Dinv g3)}dt. With source unnormalized norms and ||g||_Xsrc=||g||_(L^infinity L2src)+||g'||_(L^infinity Hsrc^(-23/14)), the source gives ||Csrc||_(L2src)<=C*(b_s-a_s)*product_j||g_j||_Xsrc+C*||g_i||_(L^infinity Hsrc^(-23/14))*product_(j!=i)||g_j||_(L^infinity L2src) for each i=1,2,3. If the three inputs are time-independent then ||Csrc||_(L2src)<=C_alpha_s*(b_s-a_s)^alpha_s*product_j||g_j||_(Hsrc^alpha_s). Constants are independent of interval location and Fourier support.

For time-independent mean-zero g1,g2 in Hsrc^sigma_s define Fsrc_j(t;g1,g2)=(1/2)integral_(t_j)^t exp(s partial_x^3)*partial_x[(exp(-s partial_x^3)g1)(exp(-s partial_x^3)g2)]ds. source.statement: Let 0<sigma_s<=1, tau_s>0, t_j=j*tau_s>=0 and t in [t_j,t_j+tau_s]. For time-independent mean-zero g1,g2 in Hsrc^sigma_s define Fsrc_j(t;g1,g2)=(1/2)integral_(t_j)^t exp(s partial_x^3)*partial_x[(exp(-s partial_x^3)g1)(exp(-s partial_x^3)g2)]ds. With beta0=2*sigma_s-3/2 for sigma_s<1/2, beta0=-1/2-epsilon for sigma_s=1/2 (any fixed sufficiently small epsilon>0), and beta0=sigma_s-1 for sigma_s>1/2, the source gives, for beta in [beta0,1+sigma_s], ||Fsrc_j(t;g1,g2)||_(Hsrc^beta)<=C*tau_s^((1+sigma_s-beta)/(1+sigma_s-beta0))*||g1||_(Hsrc^sigma_s)*||g2||_(Hsrc^sigma_s), with C depending only on exponents (and epsilon) and uniform in j,tau_s,t and support. Its endpoint formula is (1/6)[S_(-s) Pnz((S_s Dinv g1)(S_s Dinv g2))]_(s=t_j)^(s=t).

record.statement: For sigma_s in [0,1], ||g*h||_(L2src)<=C_sigma_s ||g||_(Hsrc^sigma_s)||h||_(Hsrc^a(sigma_s)), where a(0)=1/2+epsilon, a(sigma_s)=1/2-sigma_s for 0<sigma_s<1/2, a(1/2)=epsilon, and a(sigma_s)=0 for 1/2<sigma_s<=1, with any fixed sufficiently small epsilon>0 at the indicated endpoints. The functions are arbitrary periodic functions in these two spaces; constants depend only on the chosen exponents.

record.statement: There is A=A(T,gamma,R)<infinity such that every real mean-zero initial datum f0 in H^gamma with ||f0||_(H^gamma)<=R has a unique exact KdV solution in the convention D012 and sup_[0,T]||u(t)||_(H^gamma)<=A. Smooth initial data give smooth solutions, with the same H^gamma bound. Thus the twisted v=S_(-t)u obeys M<=1+A uniformly on this ball. For any B>0, two real mean-zero initial L2 data with norm sum <=B have flows satisfying sup_[0,T]||u-tilde u||_2<=C(T,B)||u0-tilde u0||_2. In particular real mean-zero Fourier polynomial approximations to H^gamma data converge in C([0,T];L2) to this solution.

For tau>0 and real alpha,beta, eta_tau=0 if alpha*beta=0; otherwise |eta_tau|<=2 min(|alpha/beta|,|beta/alpha|) and |eta_tau|<=tau min(|alpha|,|beta|). For nonzero integers a+b+c+d=0, with decreasing magnitudes N1>=N2>=N3>=N4, one has N1<=3N2 and, putting A=|ab|,B=|cd|, (1/|d|)min(A/B,B/A)<=3/N3 and |a+b|/max(A,B)<=6/N3.

For all nonnegative sequences x1,x2,x3,x4 in ell^2(Z\{0}), sum_(a+b+c+d=0,abcd!=0) x1(a)x2(b)x3(c)x4(d)/Third(a,b,c,d)<=C product_(r=1)^4||xr||_(ell^2). The same bound holds after restricting the sum to any subset.

Remainder has a unique continuous trilinear extension from mean-zero H^sigma inputs to L2 for each 0<=sigma<=1, and ||Remainder_(t0,tau)(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_sigma*tau^(1+sigma)*product_j||fj||_(H^sigma), uniformly for all t0 real, tau>0 and Fourier support. The same estimate holds with any extra frequency multiplier of modulus <=1, including restrictions Phi=0 or Phi!=0. In particular if mean-zero w in H^gamma, mean-zero f in L2, ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0 and delta=||f-w||_2<=1, then for 0<tau<=1, ||Remainder_(t0,tau)(f,f,f)||_2<=C_(M0,gamma)*tau*(tau^gamma+delta).

S_t is an isometry on every H^s and preserves real functions and zero mean; Fourier projections contract these norms. For mean-zero L2 inputs, ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2, ||Bop_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))<=C||f||_2||g||_2, ||Jop_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2 and ||Jop_t(A,B)||_2<=C||Dinv A||_2||B||_2, uniformly in t. For arbitrary L2 F,G, ||Dinv Pnz(FG)||_2<=C||F||_2||G||_2. For mean-zero A, ||A||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A||_2. H^1 embeds continuously into L^infinity and satisfies ||AB||_(H^1)<=C||A||_(H^1)||B||_(H^1). For time-smooth spatially smooth mean-zero f,g on [a,b], integral_a^b Bop_t(f,g)dt=(1/3)[Jop_t(f,g)]_a^b-(1/3)integral_a^b[Jop_t(f',g)+Jop_t(f,g')]dt. Also Jop is symmetric and integral_I Jop_t(Bop_t(f,g),h)dt=Cop_I(f,g,h). These identities hold piecewise in time and add across adjoining steps with their common endpoints. For every fixed tau>0, Ftau:L2_zero->H^1 and Psi_tau:L2_zero->L2_zero are continuous polynomial maps, preserve reality, and map smooth data to smooth data; all finite iterates are therefore well defined and continuous in L2.

Constants are uniform in interval location and Fourier support.

For 0<tau<=1, n>=0, t in [n*tau,(n+1)*tau] and mean-zero w in H^gamma with ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0, sup_t||Stage_n(t;w)||_(H^agamma)<=C_(M0,gamma)*tau^gamma and sup_t||Stage_n(t;w)||_(H^(1+gamma))<=C_(M0,gamma). Also ||fg||_2<=C_gamma||f||_(H^gamma)||g||_(H^agamma) for all f,g in these spaces, without mean restrictions. All constants are independent of n,tau and support.

record.statement: For any smooth real mean-zero datum and integer L>=1, tau=T/L, the scheme iterates are smooth, real and mean-zero. With D023 on each step, v^(n+1)=f_n+F_n(t_(n+1))+C_n(t_(n+1))-Remainder_(t_n,tau)(f_n,f_n,f_n). Hence V(t_n)=v^n and V(t_(n+1))=v^(n+1), so V is continuous and piecewise smooth on [0,T]. Also Y_n'=Bop_t(f_n,F_n)+(1/2)Bop_t(F_n,F_n)-W_n/tau, Y_n(t_n)=0, and Rres is continuous, piecewise smooth with Rres'= -Bop_t(Y_n,z_n)-(1/2)Bop_t(Y_n,Y_n)-W_n/tau; consequently V'=(1/2)Bop_t(V,V)+Rres' on each step and distributionally globally. All V,Y_n,z_n,Rres and W_n are mean-zero.

Fix any step n, 0<tau<=1, a mean-zero numerical state f_n in L2 and mean-zero w in H^gamma with ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0. Define delta_n=||f_n-w||_2<=1 and q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n; use the step formulas D023 with this f_n, initially smooth. Then q_n<=2, ||f_n||_2<=M0+1, sup||F_n||_(H^1)<=C_(M0,gamma), sup||F_n-Stage_n(t;w)||_(H^1)<=C_(M0,gamma)*delta_n, sup||F_n||_(H^agamma)+sup||F_n||_2<=C_(M0,gamma)*q_n, and ||z_n||_X(I_n)<=C_(M0,gamma). Moreover sup||Bop_t(F_n,F_n)||_2<=C_(M0,gamma)*q_n, sup||Q_n||_2+||W_n||_2<=C_(M0,gamma)*tau*q_n, and sup||Dinv Bop_t(f_n,F_n)||_2<=C_(M0,gamma)*q_n. Suprema are over the step; constants are uniform in the step and support.

Under the step hypotheses explicitly stated below, with smooth states initially and the interpolation D023, sup_(I_n)||Dinv Y_n'||_2<=C_(M0,gamma) q_n, sup_(I_n)||Dinv Y_n||_2<=C_(M0,gamma) tau q_n, sup_(I_n)||Y_n||_2<=C_(M0,gamma) q_n, ||Y_n||_X(I_n)<=C_(M0,gamma) q_n and sup_(I_n)||Y_n||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(M0,gamma) tau q_n. These estimates are uniform in step and Fourier support. Here explicitly the hypotheses are 0<tau<=1, n>=0, mean-zero f_n in L2 and w in H^gamma, ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0 and delta_n=||f_n-w||_2<=1, q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n.

For smooth real mean-zero initial data, 0<tau=T/L<=1 and an exact twisted solution v with sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, use D023 and suppose delta_n=||v^n-v(t_n)||_2<=1 at a step. Then sup_(I_n)||rho_n||_2<=C_(M0,gamma) tau q_n and ||Rres'||_(L^infinity(I_n;H^(-pstar)))<=C_(M0,gamma) q_n. For any I=[a,b] subset [0,T] starting at a grid point and having h=b-a<=1, define E_I=sup_I||e||_2 for e=v-V. If E_I<=1, then sup_(t in I)||Rres(t)-Rres(a)||_2<=C_(M0,gamma)(h+tau)(tau^gamma+E_I), ||e||_X(I)<=C_(M0,gamma)(tau^gamma+E_I), and ||v||_X(I)+||V||_X(I)<=C_(M0,gamma). The interval may end inside a step.

For smooth exact and numerical flows defined in D023 on [0,T] with sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, 0<tau=T/L<=1, let I=[a,b] start at a grid point, h=b-a<=1, E_I=sup_I||v-V||_2<=1. Set e=v-V, g=v-e/2 and F_I(t)=integral_a^t Bop_s(e,g)ds. Then e(t)=e(a)+F_I(t)-(Rres(t)-Rres(a)). For every N>=2, sup_I||P_leq(N)F_I||_2<=C N^2 h E_I and sup_I||P_gt(N)F_I||_2<=C(h+tau)tau^gamma+C(h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))E_I. Consequently E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C(h+tau)tau^gamma+C(N^2 h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))E_I. Constants depend only on M0,gamma (and the fixed final horizon) and are uniform in Fourier support, restart a and step size.

record.statement: There exist C>0 and tau0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that for every smooth real mean-zero u0 with ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every integer L>=1, tau=T/L<=tau0, the interpolation D023 satisfies sup_[0,T]||S_(-t)u(t)-V(t)||_2<=C tau^gamma. Hence max_(0<=n<=L)||u(n*tau)-u^n||_2<=C tau^gamma for all these smooth data, uniformly in all higher Sobolev norms and Fourier support.

There exist positive constants C and tau0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that, for every real mean-zero u0 in H^gamma(Ttor) with ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0, the exact KdV solution in D012 exists and the unmodified unfiltered scheme D009–D011 is well defined and satisfies max_(0<=n<=L)||u(n*tau)-u^n||_(L2)<=C*tau^gamma. These constants are uniform on the entire initial-data ball, all permitted timesteps, and all Fourier supports, with the domain, normalized measure, Fourier/Sobolev conventions, Airy group, projections, inverse derivatives and full Ftau,Htau formula fixed in D001–D012.
